levels.descriptor: Expert: fully satisfies all demands with precise, sophisticated and effortless control; extremely rare minor slips only.
Very good: covers all demands well with wide, flexible and precise control; only occasional unsystematic slips.
Good: covers demands with clear logic and varied control; some awareness of sophisticated language despite occasional inappropriacy.
Competent: generally addresses demands with adequate range but limited flexibility; errors and mechanical linking do not block meaning.
Modest: partly addresses demands with limited range and frequent errors in organisation, vocabulary and grammar; meaning often strained.
Limited: minimal response with poor organisation, very restricted vocabulary and grammar; frequent misunderstanding and difficulty following.
Extremely limited: barely conveys ideas with little organisation and severe language control problems.
Intermittent: isolated words or memorised phrases with almost no coherent communication.
Non-user: essentially no language beyond a few isolated words.
No assessable response: blank, wholly copied/plagiarised, or unrelated to any prompt.

dimensions.label: Task Response
dimensions.ask: Does the essay fully answer all parts of the prompt with a clear position, well-extended relevant ideas and supported evidence in 250+ words of connected essay form?

dimensions.label: Coherence and Cohesion
dimensions.ask: Is the essay logically organised with clear progression, effective paragraphing, sequencing and varied appropriate linking and referencing?

dimensions.label: Lexical Resource
dimensions.ask: Is vocabulary wide, precise and appropriate with good collocation and spelling, including less common and idiomatic use where suitable?

dimensions.label: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
dimensions.ask: Is there a wide flexible range of sentence structures with accurate grammar and punctuation and frequent error-free sentences?

rubric.notes: Restated from IELTS Writing key assessment criteria and Task 2 band descriptors (May 2023). Each of the four criteria is weighted equally for Task 2. Penalise memorised/formulaic responses, bullet points or note form, off-topic irrelevance, underlength below 250 words, and partly or wholly plagiarised text.

Why is shopping so popular? What effects does its increase in popularity have on individuals and society?
What form do these problems take? Do the problems outweigh the benefits?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of...?
Is this a positive or negative development?
